$description: Per-action_type templates for composing Zuora Workflow tasks. Each entry contains description, hooks, a fully-formed template with sentinel slots, required_params, required_at_import, param_enums, boolean_string_params, and (for Tier-1 tasks) data_contract.Sentinel tokens: <<TASK_ID>>, <<UPSTREAM_TASK_ID_OR_NULL>>, <<TOP>>, <<LEFT>>, <<REQUIRED:...>>. The linter fails on any unreplaced <<...>> token.

$data_contract_schema.$description: Per-task contract describing what the task adds to Data.* for downstream tasks (writes), what Data.X.Y references it consumes from upstream (reads), and how predictable that output is at design time. The linter walks the task graph topologically using these contracts to validate Liquid {{ Data.X.Y }} references (rules E170/W171/W172/W173/W174). For non-Tier-1 tasks without a contract, the linter falls back to $default_data_contract.
$data_contract_schema.predictability: One of: 'deterministic' (scope and field shape both fully known: Query, Create, Update, CustomObject::Query, amendments), 'semi-deterministic' (scope known, field shape partial or large/standardized: Export, Billing::BillRun, Payment::PaymentRun, GraphQuery, Logic::Liquid, Approval, Reporting::*, file-handling tasks), 'opaque' (scope known but field shape unknowable until runtime: Callout, AsynchronousCallout, Logic::Lambda, Script::JavaScript, Logic::JSONTransform, Logic::XMLTransform, Logic::CSVTranslator, Logic::ResponseFormatter, Execute::WorkflowTask, Mediation::SendEvents), 'scoping' (no positive writes; routes execution and/or rebinds existing scopes: If, Logic::Case, Iterate, Logic::Merge, Approval, Delete, CustomObject::Delete), 'none' (side-effect-only or non-data tasks: Email, Notifications::SMS, Notifications::Kafka, Delay, UI::Page, UI::Stop, Upload::*, UsageMediation::*, File::FileOperations file-only modes).

writes.fields: comma-separated field names, or from_param:<paramPath>, or OPAQUE, or LIQUID_SCOPE
writes.notes: optional human note

$data_contract_schema.opaque: true if downstream cannot statically know writes[].fields (Callout, Lambda, JS, JSONTransform, XMLTransform, AsyncCallout). The linter emits W172 for downstream Data.<placement>.<field> references unless the opaque task carries a parameters._opaque_trusted='true' or parameters._expected_response_schema={...} sentinel.
$data_contract_schema.opaque_prompt_required: true if the build skill must prompt the user (Step 3e) before composing downstream tasks that reference this task's scope. Mirrors opaque=true for Callout, AsynchronousCallout, Logic::Lambda, Logic::Script::JavaScript, Execute::WorkflowTask, Logic::JSONTransform, Logic::XMLTransform, Logic::CSVTranslator, Logic::ResponseFormatter, Mediation::SendEvents.
$data_contract_schema.rebinds: object key whose Array binding becomes a single Hash inside the For-Each branch (Iterate only). Inside that branch downstream tasks read Data.<rebound>.<Field> for the current row. Outside the branch the original Array binding (or Merge result) returns.
$data_contract_schema.routing_only: true for tasks that only branch (If, Logic::Case, Approval, Delay) — no writes, but reads still apply via parameters.if_clause / case_clause. Used together with predictability='scoping' or 'none'.
$data_contract_schema.fields_partial_known: true when the writes scope is known but the per-row keys are extracted from a free-form param (e.g. GraphQuery selection set, Logic::Liquid assigns). Linter downgrades W171 to a notice.

$sentinel_keys_in_parameters._opaque_trusted: Set to 'true' (string) on Callout/Async/Lambda/JS/etc. to suppress W172 across all downstream references. Unknown keys are ignored at import (composer/linter metadata only).
$sentinel_keys_in_parameters._expected_response_schema: JSON object documenting the expected response shape (e.g. { 'Invoice': { 'Id': 'string', 'Number': 'string' } }). When set, the linter performs field-level checks on Data.<scope>.<field> references for that opaque scope as if it were deterministic.

$default_data_contract.$description: Fallback contract for any action_type not present in this catalog (or for Tier-1 entries without a data_contract block). Treated as opaque: writes nothing the linter can validate, downstream Data.<TaskAction>.* references emit W172. Composer should add an explicit data_contract or _data_contract annotation when known.

$configuration_contract_schema.$description: Per-task contract describing how each parameters.* field is sourced in the Workflow UI and which fields are accepted on import. The composer/build skill consults this contract to (a) only emit declared fields, (b) prompt for fields whose source is describe-call or user-input, and (c) skip fields whose visible_when predicate evaluates false against sibling parameters. Linter rules W178 (UI-only-leak) and W177 (undeclared-describe-field) reference these contracts.

field_schema.$field: Dotted path under the task envelope. Most common is `parameters.<name>`; for top-level columns use `<columnName>` (e.g. `object`, `object_id`, `task_id`).
field_schema.purpose: One-line explanation of what this field controls at runtime.
field_schema.source: How the UI populates the value. One of: user-input (free-form text/number), dropdown-static (hard-coded options), dropdown-static-from-enums (options from Workflow enums), dropdown-from-parent-task (options from upstream task data/object structure — e.g. Iterate.object), describe-call (options from live Zuora describe — e.g. Export/Query/Create/Update parameters.fields), derive-from-workflow-parameters (auto-derived from workflow.parameters.fields), callout-response-field (set at runtime, not user-configurable), computed (auto-set; never user-supplied), code-editor (Liquid/JS/SQL), repeated-row (repeating row form — e.g. Email recipients, Callout headers), boolean-checkbox (checkbox; persisted as "true"/"false" strings — see boolean_string_params).
field_schema.options_source: When source is dropdown-* or describe-call: short pointer to where the UI gets its options (e.g. Workflow call_type enum, parent task Files keys, live describe). Omit when irrelevant.
field_schema.required_when: Liquid-ish predicate against sibling parameters that makes this field required (e.g. `parameters.body_type == 'raw'` for Callout.parameters.raw_body). When omitted, the field is either always required (see template `<<REQUIRED>>` markers) or always optional.
field_schema.visible_when: Liquid-ish predicate against sibling parameters that makes this field visible in the UI. When omitted, the field is always visible. The composer should drop fields whose predicate is false (otherwise they can confuse the runtime).
field_schema.default: Default value the Workflow UI seeds when the field is left blank. Match the literal type persisted on import (string "true" for booleans, integer for chunk_size, etc.).
field_schema.notes: Any extra constraints not captured above (cross-field rules, gotchas, deprecated keys).

$configuration_contract_schema.$design_intent: These contracts are the truth source for: (a) the zuora-workflow-build skill per-task UX (which fields to ask for vs infer); (b) the linter W177/W178 rules; (c) the composer allowlist of import-accepted fields. They are NOT a runtime schema — runtime writes live in data_contract.

fields.notes: Each entry can be a literal email or a Liquid expression like `{{Data.Account.WorkEmail__c}}`.

Reply-To address.
fields.notes: Required when from is workflow@zuora.com on non-Zuora orgs.

fields.notes: Top-level on the form, but in import JSON the canonical place is parameters.headers_attributes.

Email.notes: email.from is required unless email.preview_only is 'true'. Liquid template should reference Data scopes: {{Data.Account.Name}}, {{Data.Invoice.Number}}, etc.

Export.description: Export a Zuora object via SOAP export (bulk CSV).

writes.notes: Export streams CSV results to file storage; downstream Iterate(object=<file_holder_name>) processes the rows. The selected fields parameters.fields[<object>][] become the CSV headers and per-row keys when iterated. Inside that Iterate body, Data.<object>.<Field> is field-level resolvable from parameters.fields.
Export also stores a small reference object at Data.Export[<object>].

fields.purpose: Zuora SOAP-exportable object name (e.g. Invoice, Account, Subscription).
fields.options_source: @appinstance.live describe.keys filtered by export support (see Workflow + Workflow). Composer should call mcp__zuora-mcp describe before populating.

fields.purpose: Per-object map of selected fields and their aggregation/output mode.
fields.options_source: @appinstance.live describe filtered to entries where v[:selectable] == 'true' AND v[:context].include?('export'). Related objects via describe_helper :related_objects.
fields.notes: Value per field is one of "true" | "Min" | "Max" | "Count" | "Sum" | "Average". Sum/Average only valid for numeric fields (decimal/integer per Workflow). Composer must NEVER invent field names -- always derive from describe. At least one field must be selected.

fields.purpose: Export ZOQL filter appended after `Where`. Liquid-evaluated.
fields.notes: Use Export ZOQL syntax (joins via Object.Field). Liquid in `{{Data.X.Y}}` interpolates at runtime. Never include `Where` keyword -- Workflow prepends it.

fields.purpose: Seconds to wait after enqueue before issuing the SOAP create -- gives Zuora data-source replication time to catch up.
fields.default: 0 (60 on persisted records when blank, see)
fields.notes: Persist as integer or numeric string. Runtime waits up to this many seconds before the export query. Must be <= 60 seconds.

fields.purpose: When 'true', request a Zuora encrypted export.
When 'true', request a zipped CSV export.
When 'true', stop downstream tasks if the Export returned 0 rows.

Export.notes: At least one field selected for the configured object. Each selected field value must be the STRING 'true'. Server-side query_test / export_test hits the live tenant at save time but is skipped on import (import does not run form validations).

Query.description: Query a Zuora object via SOAP Query (max 2000 records).

writes.notes: Each Hash row contains the keys selected in parameters.fields[<object>]. Inside an Iterate(object=<placement|object>) For-Each branch, Data.<placement|object> rebinds to a single Hash (one row).

fields.purpose: Zuora SOAP-queryable object name.
fields.options_source: @appinstance.live describe.keys filtered by query support (see Workflow + Workflow). Composer should run mcp__zuora-mcp describe before populating.

fields.purpose: Per-object selection of returned columns.
fields.options_source: @appinstance.live describe filtered to entries where v[:selectable] == 'true' AND v[:context].include?('select'). Related objects via :related_objects.
fields.notes: Value per field is the literal STRING "true". Composer must NEVER invent field names -- always derive from the describe response. At least one field must be selected.

fields.purpose: ZOQL WHERE clause appended after `Where`. Liquid-evaluated.
fields.notes: Use Query ZOQL (joins via Object.Field). Liquid `{{Data.X.Y}}` interpolates at runtime. Do NOT include the keyword `Where` -- Workflow prepends it.

fields.purpose: Override the Data scope name (default: self.object).
fields.notes: Use when two Query tasks target the same object and you need to disambiguate. Downstream Liquid must reference Data.<placement>. Iterate.object should match this value.

fields.purpose: Cap on rows returned by the SOAP query.
fields.notes: For more than 2000 rows use Export instead of Query.

fields.purpose: When 'true', allow downstream tasks to run even if Query returned 0 rows; when 'false', stop the workflow.

Query.notes: Results stored into Data.<object> (or Data.<placement> if placement parameter is set). For more than 2000 records use Export or GraphQuery.

GraphQuery.description: Query Zuora data via the GraphQL API with variables.

writes.notes: Shape is the parsed GraphQL response under data.<baseObject>. Linter does not parse GraphQL; treats fields as 'best-effort' opaque inside the placement bucket.

GraphQuery.notes: query is a GraphQL string; variables is a JSON-encoded string (not an object).

Iterate.description: Iterate over a data collection; emit a 'For Each' linkage per row.

template.name: Iterate
template.object: <<REQUIRED: Data key to iterate over, e.g. Invoice, or CUSTOM LIQUID>>

reads.notes: Must be the name of an Array<Hash> or File key already present in Data, OR the literal 'CUSTOM LIQUID' (with parameters.liquid_statement).

data_contract.rebinds: Inside the For Each linkage branch, Data.{object} rebinds to a single Hash (one row) for the duration of that branch. After Complete, downstream tasks see the original Array binding (or the merged result of inner-loop writes).

fields.purpose: Source of the iteration: a Data scope name from a parent task, the file_holder_name produced by an upstream Export / File task, or the literal 'CUSTOM LIQUID'.
fields.options_source: Workflow -- `f.select :object, options_for_select(f.object.objects,...)`. Workflow#objects walks the parent task's data_structure entries plus any Files entries, and prepends 'CUSTOM LIQUID'. Composer must therefore pick from the parent task's writes and not invent a name.
fields.notes: After an Export, the dropdown shows the file_holder_name like `Invoice__1.csv.zip`, NOT just `Invoice`. Both are valid `object` values but route to different code paths in task runtime; if you want row-level Liquid you almost always pick the file form.

fields.purpose: How to enumerate the source.
fields.notes: Unique-Field requires parameters.iteration_field; Iterate emits one branch per distinct value of that field across the parent rows.

fields.purpose: When iteration_type is Unique-Field, the column name whose distinct values drive the loop.
Number of rows per For-Each branch (chunked iteration).
fields.notes: When >1, the branch sees Data.{object} as Array<Hash> of `chunk_size` rows instead of a single Hash.

fields.purpose: When object == 'CUSTOM LIQUID', the Liquid expression that produces the iteration source.
When iterating a file, the file format.
fields.visible_when: object resolves to a Files entry (e.g. *.csv.zip from Export, *.csv from File::FileOperations)

fields.purpose: Skip the first N lines of the file as headers (CSV).
Skip a fixed-width trailer line at end of file.
Comma-separated list of CSV columns to keep; others are dropped before iteration.
When 'true', synthesize column headers (col_1, col_2,...) for header-less CSV.
File encoding for FIXED width files.
Number of lines to skip from the top of a FIXED width file.
Number of lines to skip from the bottom of a FIXED width file.
Field-name + offset + length definitions for FIXED width parsing.

When 'true', the iterated source is already an Array (e.g. parameters.liquid_statement returns JSON Array directly, or the file payload is a JSON Array). When 'false' (default), the model parses the source row-by-row.

Iterate.notes: object can be a Data key name (e.g., 'Invoice' reads Data.Invoice[]), a file label from Files, or the literal 'CUSTOM LIQUID' with parameters.liquid_statement set. Hook 'Complete' fires once after all iterations finish; NOT 'Iterate' (that is a scope name only - see linter typo hint).

If.description: Branch on a Liquid-evaluated boolean expression; emit True or False linkage.

fields.purpose: Liquid expression that must evaluate (after lowercasing and stripping) to either 'true' or 'false'. Emit capitalized True/False branch literals in the template.
fields.options_source: Free-form Liquid; UI placeholder is `{% if 0 > 1 %} True {% else %} False {% endif %}`.
fields.notes: The model lowercases and strips before comparing, so 'True' / 'FALSE' / 'true\n' all work. Any other value raises a WorkflowError at runtime. Linter flags `If` tasks with `Success` linkages (only True/False/Failure are valid).

fields.purpose: Skip the save-time Liquid parse check (use when the Liquid depends on runtime data not visible at design time).

If.notes: Example if_clause: '{% if Data.Invoice.Balance > 0 %}True{% else %}False{% endif %}'. Always emit capitalized True/False branch literals (matches the UI default). Runtime lowercases before routing, so True/False and true/false both work, but generated workflows must use True/False.

Logic::Case.description: Multi-way branch: evaluate a Liquid clause and route to the matching Case_N hook.

parameters.case_clause: <<REQUIRED: Liquid expression whose string value is matched against case_condition values>>

data_contract.branch_partitioning: Each Case_N hook produces an independent downstream subgraph. The linter (W174) flags references to scopes only produced inside one branch from a task that's downstream of a different (or all/Else) branch.

fields.purpose: Liquid expression whose stripped string value is matched against case_condition values.
fields.notes: Required; must be valid Liquid.

fields.purpose: Ordered map of `Case_N -> match value` (regex by default).
fields.notes: Keys MUST be `Case_1`, `Case_2`,... (sequential, no gaps). Linker E111/E112 flag mis-numbered keys; Workflow would silently renumber and destroy mismatched linkages. Every Case_N value must be non-blank. Keys must be sequential Case_1..Case_N (no gaps) or linkages break.

fields.purpose: When 'true', match each case value as a literal string instead of a regex.
Skip the save-time Liquid parse check.

Logic::Case.notes: ALWAYS pre-normalize case_condition keys to sequential Case_1, Case_2,..., Case_Else. Workflow Logic::Case#import/save Case key normalization renumbers the keys and DESTROYS any linkage whose linkage_type does not map to the new keys. Emit linkages with linkage_type matching case_condition keys plus optional Case_Else and Failure.

Logic::Liquid.description: Execute a Liquid template to transform or augment workflow Data.

writes.notes: Every {% assign foo =... %} or {% capture foo %} in parameters.code becomes Data.Liquid.foo for downstream tasks. The linter scans parameters.code for assign/capture tags to infer the available keys.

fields.purpose: Liquid template body. Use {% assign %} / {% capture %} to publish keys under Data.Liquid for downstream tasks.
fields.notes: Only top-level {% assign %} and {% capture %} survive into Data.Liquid; values rendered with {{... }} but not assigned are discarded. Linter scans this field to populate the W173 catalogue of producible scopes.

fields.purpose: Override the destination key under Data.Liquid (or under Data when used with the standard placement convention).
fields.notes: Optional. The W170 family enforces unique placement values across sibling Liquid tasks.

fields.purpose: No-op for Logic::Liquid because no save-time validation runs; included for API symmetry.

Logic::Liquid.notes: Result placement: if parameters.placement is set, output goes to Data.Liquid.<placement>; otherwise Data.Liquid. Liquid syntax errors are caught at RUN time, not import - form save validation does not parse the Liquid.

Logic::Merge.description: Merge multiple branches back into a single path after a For-Each/Case fan-out.

writes.notes: merge_data_from_branches deep-merges Workflow/Files/Liquid keys; concatenates arrays; mixes other clashing values into arrays. Linter takes set-union of predecessor available_data on the Success linkage.

data_contract.branch_partitioning: Logic::Merge consolidates available scopes from all inbound branches; downstream tasks see the UNION.

fields.purpose: Logic::Merge has NO user-configurable parameters; the partial is intentionally blank. Only the workflow graph topology controls behaviour.

Logic::Merge.notes: CONSTRAINT: no 'For Each' linkage may appear on any directed path from the workflow start to this Merge task. Workflow enforces For-Each-before-Merge at save time and rewrites merge metadata server-side — do not attempt to populate merge_start/merge_paths client-side.

template.name: XMLTransform

parameters.template: <<REQUIRED when mode='to_xml': XSLT 1.0/2.0 stylesheet with <xsl:output method='xml|csv|txt|html'/>>

CustomObject::Create.description: Create a Custom Object record. parameters.fields is a NESTED hash: parameters.fields.<self.object>.<FieldName> = <value>. Do NOT put fields flat under parameters.fields (Workflow digs fields[self.object] only and treats a flat map as empty). object is `<namespace>__<object>` WITHOUT a trailing `__c` (e.g. default__Vendor, never default__Vendor__c — Workflow namespace/object split on __ would parse object_name as 'c'). There is NO placement parameter; output always lands at Data.<self.object>. Field names MUST exist in the Custom Object schema.

configuration_contract.$anti_patterns: Do NOT use SOAP Create shape (flat parameters.fields). Do NOT append __c to object. Do NOT invent parameters.placement — Create always writes Data.<object>. Do NOT put the record id in parameters.id.

fields.purpose: Custom Object API name (`<namespace>__<object>`, e.g. `default__Vendor`). NEVER end with `__c` — that is a field suffix; Workflow splits the object name on `__`, so `default__Vendor__c` becomes object_name=`c`.
fields.options_source: tenant Workflow app instance get_entity_id) -> {namespace: {object: schema}}
fields.notes: Use namespace__object without a trailing __c. Required schema __c fields must be supplied on create.

CustomObject::Query.description: Query Custom Object records via Lucene `parameters.query` and/or an `parameters.ids=...&ids=...` URL fragment. Output is written as an Array<Hash> at `Data.<alternate_location | object>` (write_data with overwrite=true, so it REPLACES any prior binding at that scope). Use parameters.alternate_location — NOT parameters.placement (that is the SOAP Query param; CustomObject::Query ignores placement). object is `<namespace>__<object>` WITHOUT a trailing `__c`. At least one of query or ids must be present. Idempotent.

parameters.query: <<OPTIONAL: Lucene filter expression (Liquid OK), e.g. `Status__c:Submitted`. At least one of query|ids required>>
parameters.alternate_location: <<OPTIONAL: alternate Data.* placement; defaults to self.object. NOT 'placement'.>>

template.object: <<REQUIRED: Custom Object API name (e.g. default__Vendor — NOT default__Vendor__c)>>

writes.notes: write_data(object_name: payload_location, object_data: records, overwrite: true) - REPLACES any prior Hash/Array at that scope. Inside an Iterate For-Each branch over this scope, the binding rebinds to a single Hash row. payload_location = parameters.alternate_location || self.object (Workflow) — parameters.placement is ignored.

configuration_contract.$anti_patterns: Do NOT use parameters.placement (SOAP Query). Use parameters.alternate_location. Do NOT append __c to object.

Notifications::Kafka.description: Send a message to a Kafka topic (internal access only).

data_contract.$notes: Pure side-effect (publishes to Kafka); writes nothing to Data.*.

Execute::WorkflowTask.description: Invoke another workflow as a subroutine.

writes.notes: Sub-workflow's exposed return payload (depends on the target workflow_id and what its final tasks publish). The linter cannot statically inspect another workflow definition.

Approval.description: Human-in-the-loop approval step with Approve/Reject branches; supports zuoraInbox / email / slack / webex / teams delivery channels.

approver_emails: <<REQUIRED: Zuora username or '*' for any user>>

writes.notes: After the approver/rejecter responds, task runtime writes {action, user, data} to Data.Approval (Workflow/). 'data' is the optional approvalData captured from the approve/reject API call.

data_contract.branch_partitioning: Approve and Reject hooks split downstream paths; Data.Approval is set on whichever branch fires.

fields.purpose: Notification channel for the approver.
Zuora usernames allowed to approve (zuoraInbox mode). Use '*' to allow any user.
fields.source: user-input (multi-tag select pre-populated with current entity's Zuora users)
fields.notes: Liquid expressions are supported -- entries containing `{{... }}` are template_parsed, then split on commas.

fields.purpose: Liquid-rendered free-form note shown to approvers (and used as Kafka message description for business-process workflows).

Teams app client secret.
Teams sender username.
Teams sender password.

Sender address used when delivery_method == 'email'.
Subject line for the email approval request.

Upload::FTP.description: Upload files to an FTP server.

data_contract.$notes: Pure side-effect (uploads files to FTP); no Data.* writes.

Upload::SFTP.description: Upload files to an SFTP server.

data_contract.$notes: Pure side-effect (uploads files to SFTP); no Data.* writes.

Upload::S3.description: Upload files to an S3 bucket.

data_contract.$notes: Pure side-effect (uploads files to S3); no Data.* writes.

Download::SFTP.description: Download files from an SFTP server.

writes.notes: Each file at parameters.remote_path is registered under Data.Files for downstream tasks (Email, Upload, Attachment, File::*) to consume.

Download::S3.description: Download files from an S3 bucket.

writes.notes: Each S3 object at parameters.s3_path is registered under Data.Files for downstream consumption.

UsageMediation::Source.description: Source step in a usage mediation pipeline.

data_contract.$notes: Usage mediation pipelines stream data row-by-row through internal channels - not via Data.*. The agent should not attempt Liquid {{ Data.X }} resolution across mediation steps.

UsageMediation::Source.notes: Usage mediation tasks use lowercase hooks 'next' and 'error' - differs from Success/Failure used elsewhere.

UsageMediation::Watermark.description: Watermark step in a usage mediation pipeline.

data_contract.$notes: Mediation pipeline step (streamed); no Data.* writes.

UsageMediation::Filter.description: Filter step in a usage mediation pipeline.

data_contract.$notes: Mediation pipeline filter step (streamed); no Data.* writes.

UsageMediation::Map.description: Map step in a usage mediation pipeline.

data_contract.$notes: Mediation pipeline mapping step (streamed); no Data.* writes.

UsageMediation::Group.description: Group/aggregate step in a usage mediation pipeline.

data_contract.$notes: Mediation pipeline group/aggregate step (streamed); no Data.* writes.

UsageMediation::Sink.description: Sink step in a usage mediation pipeline.

data_contract.$notes: Mediation pipeline sink (publishes to downstream); no Data.* writes.

Mediation::SendEvents.description: Send mediated events to a downstream system.

writes.notes: Downstream mediation API response (acks/ids vary). Treat as opaque - declare _expected_response_schema if downstream tasks need to read it.
